questions.question: Describe five special rights that children have under section 28 of the Constitution.
questions.expected_answer: Every child has the right to a name and nationality from birth; to family or parental care, or suitable alternative care; to basic nutrition, shelter, basic health care and social services; to be protected from maltreatment, neglect, abuse or degradation; and to be protected from exploitative labour. A child may be detained only as a last resort, separately from adults, and a child's best interests are of paramount importance in every matter concerning the child.

questions.question: Explain how the Children's Charter of South Africa was created and what it called for.
questions.expected_answer: In 1992, while apartheid was being negotiated away, an international summit on children's rights was held in Cape Town, and children from many communities across South Africa took part. They discussed their problems and drew up the charter, written mainly by children themselves. It called for equal treatment, protection from violence and abuse, including by police and security forces, family life, free and equal education, health care, housing, food and water, play, protection from child labour and the right to be heard.

questions.question: Explain three responsibilities that children have, linking each to a right.
questions.expected_answer: With the right to education, children should go to school regularly, do their best and respect teachers and classmates. With the right to be protected from abuse, children should not bully, hurt or insult others. With the right to a healthy environment, children should not litter and should save water and electricity. With the right to express opinions, they should listen to others and disagree respectfully.
